$comment: Phase 32A. Quotes for every grazingRestrictions value on herbicide, insecticide and fungicide plugins, keyed pluginId → fact path (grazeDays, hayDays, lactatingDairyGrazeDays, meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays, notForPasture, manureCarryover, speciesExceptions.<speciesId>[.lactating].grazeDays|hayDays). Each entry is { url, publisher, date, quote, note? } read from the product label. `pastureAllowlist` lists pasture-labelled products that have no grazingRestrictions yet, each with a reason. The gate in apps/web/src/lib/plugins/sourceCoverage.gate.test.ts fails on a pasture-labelled product that is neither covered nor listed, and on a listed product that is no longer a gap.

grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.

hayDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
hayDays.note: The label sets no hay interval; the 14 days is advice for weed control. Recorded as 14 (stricter reading) rather than 0.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label names no separate interval for lactating dairy animals and its no-restriction grazing statement has no dairy exception, so 0.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: There are no restrictions on grazing or grass hay harvest intervals following application of Chaparral at labeled rates. However, cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds will reduce weed control. Wait 14 days after herbicide application to cut grass hay to allow herbicide to work.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: The label states no slaughter withdrawal anywhere and says there are no grazing interval restrictions, so 0. The grazing statement is the only support; no sentence says 'no slaughter restriction'.

manureCarryover.quote: Do not plant a broadleaf crop in fields treated in the previous year with manure from animals that have grazed forage or eaten hay harvested from treated areas until an adequately sensitive field bioassay is conducted to determine that the aminopyralid concentration in the soil is at level that is not injurious to the crop to be planted.

grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Except for lactating dairy animals, there are no grazing restrictions following application of this product.

hayDays.quote: Do not harvest hay for 14 days after application.
hayDays.note: Same 14 days in the Rangeland and Permanent Pastures section: 'Do not cut forage for hay within 14 days of application.' The label also says the product may not be applied to forage that is to be cut and sold for commercial purposes.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Grazing Lactating Dairy Animals: Do not allow lactating dairy animals to graze treated areas until the next growing season following application of this product.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label gives no day count. Recorded as 365 days, the stricter reading of 'until the next growing season'.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Slaughter Restrictions: During the season of application, withdraw livestock from grazing treated grass at least 3 days before slaughter.

manureCarryover.quote: Animals that have been fed triclopyr treated forage must be fed forage free of triclopyr for at least 3 days before movement to an area where manure may be collected, or sensitive crops are grown.
manureCarryover.note: The label also bars selling or moving treated plant material, or manure from animals that grazed it, off-site for compost or bedding/feed for 30 days after application.

grazeDays.quote: DO NOT feed, graze, or harvest alfalfa or clover for 30 days following an application of Pursuit to alfalfa or clover.
grazeDays.note: Interval is for alfalfa and clover. The birdsfoot trefoil section also says 30 days; the Clearfield corn section says 45 days for corn forage, silage, fodder and grain, which is not a pasture use.

hayDays.quote: DO NOT feed, graze, or harvest alfalfa or clover for 30 days following an application of Pursuit to alfalfa or clover.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: DO NOT feed, graze, or harvest alfalfa or clover for 30 days following an application of Pursuit to alfalfa or clover.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label names no separate interval for lactating dairy animals and its 30-day no-feed/no-graze statement has no dairy exception, so the same 30 days.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: DO NOT feed, graze, or harvest alfalfa or clover for 30 days following an application of Pursuit to alfalfa or clover.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: The label states no slaughter withdrawal, so 0; animals cannot graze the treated stand for 30 days in any case. The grazing statement is the only support; no sentence says 'no slaughter restriction'.

grazeDays.quote: CROPS Alfalfa, Birdsfoot Trefoil, Clover Apply and incorporate BALAN DF before seeding.
grazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

hayDays.quote: CROPS Alfalfa, Birdsfoot Trefoil, Clover Apply and incorporate BALAN DF before seeding.
hayDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

hayDays.publisher: UPL NA / MacDermid Agricultural Solutions (EPA PPLS stamped label)
hayDays.quote: x DO NOT cut grass within 1 day of application.
hayDays.note: Grassland use restriction. Other hay intervals on this label: alfalfa forage or hay 1 day; barley/oats/triticale/wheat hay 15 days (western states only, grain 50 days, forage 3 days). Grassland governs pasture and hay-grass use, so 1 recorded; owner may prefer 15 as the stricter crop reading.

grazeDays.publisher: UPL NA / MacDermid Agricultural Solutions (EPA PPLS stamped label)
grazeDays.quote: GRASSLAND[**]: rangeland; pastures; improved pastures and similar areas used for production of native, domesticated forage grasses for harvest for livestock primarily for grazing or mechanical harvest
grazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30. The grassland section lists no grazing restriction. The only grazing statement ('DO NOT harvest cover crops for animal feed or graze livestock in treated groves') applies to citrus groves.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: GRASSLAND[**]: rangeland; pastures; improved pastures and similar areas used for production of native, domesticated forage grasses for harvest for livestock primarily for grazing or mechanical harvest
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30. No dairy statement in the grassland section.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: GRASSLAND[**]: rangeland; pastures; improved pastures and similar areas used for production of native, domesticated forage grasses for harvest for livestock primarily for grazing or mechanical harvest
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30. No slaughter statement anywhere on the label.

grazeDays.publisher: Arysta LifeScience North America (EPA PPLS stamped label, reg. 66330-276, now 70506-461)
grazeDays.quote: Animals cannot be removed from treated area for slaughter prior to 30 days after last applictions. • There is no waiting period between treatment and grazing for non-lactating dairy animals.
grazeDays.note: No waiting period before grazing by non-lactating animals (small-grain pasture statement; the pasture section's table is headed for lactating dairy animals only).

hayDays.publisher: Arysta LifeScience North America (EPA PPLS stamped label, reg. 66330-276, now 70506-461)
hayDays.quote: DICAMBA DMA 4# AG Rate per Treated Acre Up to 1 pint (1/2 Ib ail Up to 1 quart (1 Ib ail Up to 2 quarts (2 Ib ail TIMING RESTRICTIONS FOR LACTATING DAIRY ANIMALS FOLLOWING TREATMENT Days Before Grazing 7 days 21 days 40 days Days Before Hay Harvest 37 days 51 days 70 days
hayDays.note: Highest labelled rate (up to 2 quarts/acre): 70 days. 1 quart 51 days, up to 1 pint (plugin rate) 37 days. Small-grain pasture/hay section also says 'DO NOT harvest hay form treated areas before 37 days after treatment'.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.publisher: Arysta LifeScience North America (EPA PPLS stamped label, reg. 66330-276, now 70506-461)
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: DICAMBA DMA 4# AG Rate per Treated Acre Up to 1 pint (1/2 Ib ail Up to 1 quart (1 Ib ail Up to 2 quarts (2 Ib ail TIMING RESTRICTIONS FOR LACTATING DAIRY ANIMALS FOLLOWING TREATMENT Days Before Grazing 7 days 21 days 40 days Days Before Hay Harvest 37 days 51 days 70 days
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Highest labelled rate (up to 2 quarts/acre): 40 days. 1 quart 21 days, up to 1 pint (plugin rate) 7 days.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.publisher: Arysta LifeScience North America (EPA PPLS stamped label, reg. 66330-276, now 70506-461)
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Animals cannot be removed from treated area for slaughter prior to 30 days after last applictions. • There is no waiting period between treatment and grazing for non-lactating dairy animals.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Stated in the small grains (wheat, barley, oats) used for pasture or hay section; the pasture/rangeland section states no slaughter interval. Applied as the stricter reading for the whole product.

grazeDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences (EPA PPLS stamped label, GF-3850 alternate brand DuraCor)
grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. After application wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
grazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

hayDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences (EPA PPLS stamped label, GF-3850 alternate brand DuraCor)
hayDays.quote: Wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
hayDays.note: The label also states a 7-day preharvest interval ('Do not cut forage for hay within 7 days of application'); 14 days is the longer and is recorded. Hay from treated grass within the preceding 18 months may be used only on the farm or ranch where applied.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences (EPA PPLS stamped label, GF-3850 alternate brand DuraCor)
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. After application wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. After application wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

manureCarryover.publisher: Dow AgroSciences (EPA PPLS stamped label, GF-3850 alternate brand DuraCor)
manureCarryover.quote: Do not use manure from animals that have grazed forage or eaten hay harvested from treated areas within the previous 3 days, in compost, mulch, or mushroom spawn.

grazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Do not harvest forage for hay within 7 days of GrazonNext HL application. Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. Wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
grazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

hayDays.quote: Wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
hayDays.note: The label also states 'Do not harvest forage for hay within 7 days of GrazonNext HL application'; 14 days is the longer and is recorded.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Do not harvest forage for hay within 7 days of GrazonNext HL application. Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. Wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Grazing and Haying Restrictions: Do not harvest forage for hay within 7 days of GrazonNext HL application. Cutting hay too soon after spraying weeds can compromise the weed control. Wait 14 days prior to cutting grass hay to allow for maximum herbicide activity.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

manureCarryover.quote: Do not use manure from animals that have grazed forage or eaten hay harvested from treated areas within the previous 3 days, in compost, mulch or mushroom spawn.

grazeDays.quote: Do not graze or feed forage or grain from treated field corn to livestock within 30 days of application.
grazeDays.note: Cereals and soybeans: 'Allow at least 7 days between application and grazing of treated forage.' Field corn is 30 days; the longer is recorded. The label has no pasture or rangeland use.

hayDays.quote: Allow at least 30 days between application and feeding of dried hay from treated areas to livestock.
hayDays.note: Applies to dried hay from treated cereals and soybeans; the label has no pasture or grass-hay use.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Do not graze or feed forage or grain from treated field corn to livestock within 30 days of application.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label names no separate dairy interval; its livestock feeding restriction has no dairy exception, so the general 30 days is recorded.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Harvested straw may be used for bedding and/or feed.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30

grazeDays.quote: has no preharvest interval (PHI) for any crop.
grazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30. The label covers alfalfa grown for forage, hay or seed and has no grazing or haying statement; the only related sentence is the no-PHI statement.

hayDays.quote: has no preharvest interval (PHI) for any crop.
hayDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: has no preharvest interval (PHI) for any crop.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: has no preharvest interval (PHI) for any crop.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30.

grazeDays.quote: Remove domestic livestock before application and wait 8 weeks after application before grazing or harvesting.
grazeDays.note: Strictest stated interval on the label: 8 weeks (56 days) for alfalfa/clover/forage legume preplant, preemergence and renovation, and for pasture preplant, preemergence and renovation; 'Do not feed or graze treated areas for 8 weeks following application' for forage grass seed renovation. Other uses are shorter: 14 days for pasture spot and wiper applications, 36 hours for dormant and preharvest alfalfa. Recorded the longest.

hayDays.quote: Remove domestic livestock before application and wait 8 weeks after application before grazing or harvesting.
hayDays.note: Strictest stated interval on the label: 8 weeks (56 days) for alfalfa/clover/forage legume preplant, preemergence and renovation, and for pasture preplant, preemergence and renovation; 'Do not feed or graze treated areas for 8 weeks following application' for forage grass seed renovation. Other uses are shorter: 14 days for pasture spot and wiper applications, 36 hours for dormant and preharvest alfalfa. Recorded the longest. The label applies the same wait to harvesting.

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Remove domestic livestock before application and wait 8 weeks after application before grazing or harvesting.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: The label names no separate interval for lactating dairy animals; the wait applies to all domestic livestock, so 56.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Remove domestic livestock before application and wait 8 weeks after application before grazing or harvesting.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Label states no interval; recorded 0 per owner ruling 2026-09-30. The label has no slaughter statement; the quote is the closest sentence on pasture use.

grazeDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
grazeDays.quote: Do not allow livestock to graze treated areas or harvest treated corn silage as feed within 40 days after last treatment.
grazeDays.note: Longest stated interval across uses: 40 days for field corn. The rangeland and permanent grass pasture use has none ('There are no further restrictions on grazing or hay harvest following application of Stinger at labeled rates.'). Corn rate is the highest labelled rate for this restriction (2/3 pint per acre per year).

hayDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
hayDays.quote: Do not allow livestock to graze treated areas or harvest treated corn silage as feed within 40 days after last treatment.
hayDays.note: Longest stated interval across uses: 40 days for field corn. The rangeland and permanent grass pasture use has none ('There are no further restrictions on grazing or hay harvest following application of Stinger at labeled rates.'). Corn rate is the highest labelled rate for this restriction (2/3 pint per acre per year). The 40 days covers corn silage harvest; the label gives no hay number for corn, and for grain fields says 'Do not harvest hay from treated grain fields.'

lactatingDairyGrazeDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.quote: Do not permit lactating dairy animals or meat animals being finished for slaughter to forage or graze treated grain fields within 1 week after treatment.
lactatingDairyGrazeDays.note: Grain fields (wheat, barley, oats) give 1 week to lactating dairy; the 40-day corn grazing/silage wait covers all livestock and is longer, so 40 is recorded. Pasture use has no restriction.

meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.quote: Do not permit lactating dairy animals or meat animals being finished for slaughter to forage or graze treated grain fields within 1 week after treatment.
meatAnimalRemovalBeforeSlaughterDays.note: Grain fields: 1 week before slaughter. The corn grazing wait is 40 days and covers all livestock, so 40 is recorded. Pasture use has no restriction.

manureCarryover.publisher: Dow AgroSciences LLC (EPA PPLS stamped label)
manureCarryover.quote: Do not spread manure from animals that have grazed or consumed forage or hay from treated areas on land used for growing susceptible broadleaf plants or apply such materials to land used for growing broadleaf crops, ornamentals, orchards, or other susceptible desirable plants.
manureCarryover.note: Also: 'Do not transfer livestock from treated grazing areas (or feeding of treated hay) to sensitive broadleaf crop areas without first allowing 7 days of grazing on an untreated pasture (or feeding of treated hay).' and no use of hay, straw, manure or bedding straw from treated areas for composting or mulching where susceptible plants may be grown the following season.
